sites.text: André Ostertag's biodynamic estate at Epfig, now run with his son Arthur, known for the Muenchberg Riesling and for his early use of oak and his 'vins de pierre, vins de fruit, vins de temps' philosophy.

sites.name: Domaine Marcel Deiss
sites.text: Jean-Michel Deiss and his son Mathieu at Bergheim champion field-blend wines named by site rather than grape, such as Altenberg de Bergheim and Schoenenbourg, and won the right to blend in Altenberg de Bergheim.

sites.name: Domaine Albert Boxler
sites.text: A small family domaine at Niedermorschwihr known for precise, mineral Riesling from the Sommerberg and Brand grands crus.

sites.name: Château du Haut-Koenigsbourg
sites.text: The mountain castle above the vineyards of Orschwiller and Kintzheim, restored by Kaiser Wilhelm II during the German period. It overlooks the Praelatenberg grand cru and gives its name to the Coteaux du Haut-Koenigsbourg denomination.

sites.name: Eguisheim
sites.text: A medieval village built in concentric rings around the castle of Pope Leo IX, at the foot of the Eichberg and Pfersigberg grands crus.

sites.name: Riquewihr
sites.text: A walled sixteenth-century wine town, home to Hugel and Dopff au Moulin, beneath the Schoenenbourg and Sporen grands crus.

sites.name: Maison de Louis Pasteur (Arbois)
sites.text: Louis Pasteur's family house and laboratory beside the Cuisance river in Arbois, where he returned every summer. His studies of wine fermentation and spoilage in the 1860s led to his 1866 book Études sur le vin and to pasteurisation.

sites.name: Vigne de Pasteur (Rosières)
sites.text: The small vineyard at Rosières near Arbois that Pasteur bought in the 1870s for his experiments on fermentation, still in vines and now owned by the Académie des Sciences.

sites.name: Château-Chalon (village and belvedere)
sites.text: The village on its rocky spur above the vin jaune vineyards; the Belvédère Sainte-Anne gives a view over the whole appellation.

sites.name: Domaine Jean Macle
sites.text: The reference estate for Château-Chalon, run by Laurent Macle, whose vins jaunes are famous for their longevity.

sites.name: Domaine Pierre Overnoy
sites.text: Pierre Overnoy's tiny Pupillin estate, run since 2001 by Emmanuel Houillon, pioneered sulphur-free Jura wine; its Ploussard and Savagnin are among the most sought-after natural wines in the world.

sites.name: Domaine André et Mireille Tissot
sites.text: Stéphane Tissot's biodynamic estate in Arbois, with single-site Chardonnays, vin jaune, Crémant and experimental wines; one of the Jura's most influential growers.

sites.name: Fruitière Vinicole d'Arbois
sites.text: One of France's first wine co-operatives, founded in Arbois in 1906 on the model of the Jura's Comté cheese fruitières.

sites.name: Domaine Ganevat
sites.text: Jean-François Ganevat's estate at La Combe de Rotalier in the Sud Revermont, famous for dozens of single-parcel Chardonnays and Savagnins and for preserving rare old Jura grape varieties.

sites.name: Domaine Labet
sites.text: The Labet family estate at Rotalier, known for single-lieu-dit Chardonnays such as En Chalasse and Les Varrons that helped redefine ouillé Jura whites.

sites.name: Château d'Arlay
sites.text: An eighteenth-century château below the ruins of a medieval fortress, with vineyards documented since the eleventh century; known for vin jaune and Corail, a red-and-white blend.

sites.name: Abbaye de Baume-les-Messieurs
sites.text: A Benedictine abbey founded in the ninth century at the bottom of a spectacular reculée (box canyon) near Château-Chalon; its monks were early cultivators of Jura vineyards.

sites.name: Arbois
sites.text: The Jura's leading appellation around the town of Arbois, France's first AOC (1936).

sites.name: Pupillin
sites.text: The village above Arbois known as the world capital of Ploussard (Poulsard), which may add its name to Arbois.

sites.name: L'Étoile
sites.text: The white-wine appellation around the village of L'Étoile, named for its star-shaped crinoid fossils.

sites.name: Abymes
sites.text: Les Abymes (the abysses) is the chaotic field of limestone boulders left by the collapse of Mont Granier in November 1248, now planted with Jacquère that gives light, flinty whites.

sites.name: Apremont
sites.text: Apremont lies on the same Mont Granier landslide as Les Abymes, at Apremont and neighbouring communes; its Jacquère whites are crisp, floral and mineral, the best-known wine of Savoie.

sites.name: Arbin
sites.text: Arbin, on the steep slopes of the Combe de Savoie near Montmélian, is the home of Mondeuse, whose red here is dark, peppery and able to age. Louis Magnin made it famous.

sites.name: Ayze
sites.text: Ayze in the Arve valley of Haute-Savoie makes still and sparkling wine from Gringet, a grape found only here; Domaine Belluard rescued it.

sites.name: Chautagne
sites.text: Chautagne, on the slopes north of the Lac du Bourget, is known for light reds from Gamay, Pinot Noir and Mondeuse.

sites.name: Chignin
sites.text: Chignin, below the ruined towers of Chignin southeast of Chambéry, makes Jacquère whites and Mondeuse reds on limestone scree.

sites.name: Chignin-Bergeron
sites.text: Chignin-Bergeron is Savoie's richest white, made from Roussanne (locally Bergeron) on the warm, stony slopes of Chignin, Francin and Montmélian; apricot and honey with Alpine freshness.

sites.name: Cruet
sites.text: Cruet, in the Combe de Savoie, makes fresh Jacquère and Mondeuse from south-facing scree slopes.

sites.name: Crépy
sites.text: Crépy, near Lake Geneva at Ballaison, makes Chasselas whites, light and often slightly sparkling; it was a separate AOC (1948) before becoming a Vin de Savoie cru.

sites.name: Jongieux
sites.text: Jongieux, on the steep slopes above the Rhône west of the Lac du Bourget, makes whites and reds; the Marestel Roussette cru is in the same village.

sites.name: Marignan
sites.text: Marignan, on the shores of Lake Geneva at Sciez, makes light Chasselas whites.

sites.name: Marin
sites.text: Marin, near Thonon-les-Bains on Lake Geneva, makes Chasselas whites from glacial soils.

sites.name: Montmélian
sites.text: Montmélian, below the site of a great Savoyard fortress demolished by Louis XIV, makes Jacquère and Mondeuse.

sites.name: Ripaille
sites.text: Ripaille is the vineyard of the Château de Ripaille near Thonon-les-Bains on Lake Geneva, a single-estate cru of Chasselas. Its château belonged to Amadeus VIII of Savoy, who became antipope Felix V.

sites.name: Saint-Jean-de-la-Porte
sites.text: Saint-Jean-de-la-Porte, in the Combe de Savoie, is a cru for Mondeuse reds.

sites.name: Saint-Jeoire-Prieuré
sites.text: Saint-Jeoire-Prieuré, on the slopes southeast of Chambéry toward the Combe de Savoie, makes crisp Jacquère whites on limestone scree around an old Benedictine priory.

sites.name: Frangy
sites.text: Frangy in Haute-Savoie, on the Usses river near the Rhône north of Seyssel, is the northernmost Roussette cru. Its molasse and glacial slopes give fresh, floral Altesse with notes of bergamot and almond, lighter than Marestel's.

sites.name: Marestel
sites.text: Marestel, a very steep slope at Jongieux above the Rhône, is the most famous Roussette cru, giving rich, long-lived Altesse; Domaine Dupasquier is the reference.

sites.name: Monterminod
sites.text: Monterminod, on a steep limestone slope above Chambéry at Saint-Alban-Leysse, is the southernmost and smallest Roussette cru, about 16 ha delimited. Its Altesse is rich and honeyed, and suburban housing presses on its edges.

sites.name: Monthoux
sites.text: Monthoux is a small Roussette cru of about 23 ha on a sheltered limestone slope near the Lac du Bourget. Its Altesse is fine and aromatic, with quince and white flowers, and benefits from the lake's moderating influence.

sites.name: Mont Granier
sites.text: The limestone peak (1,933 m) whose north face collapsed on the night of 24 to 25 November 1248, burying villages under millions of cubic metres of rock. The debris field became the vineyards of Apremont and Les Abymes.

sites.name: Abbaye de Hautecombe
sites.text: The Cistercian abbey on the Lac du Bourget, burial place of the princes of Savoy, whose monks planted vines on the lake slopes of Chautagne and Jongieux.

sites.name: Château de Ripaille
sites.text: The fifteenth-century château of Amadeus VIII of Savoy, who became antipope Felix V, on Lake Geneva near Thonon. Its Chasselas vineyard is a single-estate Vin de Savoie cru.

sites.name: Domaine Louis Magnin
sites.text: Louis and Béatrice Magnin's estate at Arbin made Mondeuse and Chignin-Bergeron famous among sommeliers.

sites.name: Domaine Belluard
sites.text: Dominique Belluard's biodynamic estate at Ayze rescued the Gringet grape, making still and sparkling wines from it. Belluard died in 2021.

sites.name: Cerdon
sites.text: The Cerdon valley in the north of Bugey, home of the pink, sweet, ancestral-method sparkling Bugey Cerdon.

sites.name: Manicle
sites.text: A steep, south-facing limestone lieu-dit at Cheignieu-la-Balme and Pugieu near Belley, about 24 ha delimited, reserved for Chardonnay whites and Pinot Noir reds. It is the most Burgundian of Bugey's crus, giving taut, mineral whites and light, fragrant reds.

sites.name: Montagnieu
sites.text: Steep limestone slopes above the Rhône at Montagnieu, Briord and Seillonnaz, about 124 ha delimited. The cru is known for dark, peppery Mondeuse reds and for traditional-method sparkling wine based on Altesse, Chardonnay and Mondeuse; Altesse whites are sold as Roussette du Bugey Montagnieu.

sites.name: Virieu-le-Grand
sites.text: A small cru of Roussette du Bugey of about 35 ha around the village of Virieu-le-Grand in the Furans valley, for pure Altesse whites that are floral, honeyed and fresh from limestone scree.

sites.name: Mont Saint-Michel (Toul)
sites.text: The wooded limestone hill north of Toul whose slopes and the escarpment beyond hold the vineyards of the Côtes de Toul.

sites.name: Bruley
sites.text: The leading wine village of the Côtes de Toul, home to several of its producers, including Domaine Laroppe.

sites.name: Contz-les-Bains
sites.text: A village on the Moselle near the borders with Luxembourg and Germany, the northernmost zone of the French Moselle AOC.

sites.name: Vic-sur-Seille
sites.text: A historic town in the Seille valley, once the seat of the bishops of Metz, at the centre of one of the three zones of the Moselle AOC.
